doc.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025

title: Coltrane's 'Alabama' as inspiration for turning darkness into art
summary: 'Cry' is inspired by the ethos of Coltrane's 'Alabama': turning struggle into an expression of hope.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There was a line in it that I got a flash – it reminded me of “Alabama” by John Coltrane.

Yeah. Because of the story as well, and his reason for writing “Alabama” which is absolutely heart-wrenching, heartbreakingly awful and through that comes this extraordinarily beautiful expression of one man, one man and his band, and that to me is also perhaps the value of really the way of being with the awful things in the world. And I talk about this a lot with people, especially because the world’s in – there’s so much craziness. And I think people can get very disheartened and depressed. And they can find themselves in a bit of an apoplectic state or what’s the point of doing anything when the world leaders are all so monstrous. How on earth do we cope? What do we do? And I find that they sort of get in the mindset of just watching more news or sort of soaking up this terrible information. And my sense is that unless you do that consciously, and in some way use it for good, then it will suck you dry. It will absolutely suck your energy. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

And so for me seeing something like – or listening to something like “Alabama” where John Coltrane is seeing this horrific crime, and then writing this extraordinarily beautiful piece of music and expressing all of whatever he was expressing within that. For me that’s the inspiration. So what can I do with the feelings of struggle, darkness, despair. And if we as musicians, artists, whatever it is, if we can turn that darkness into something where people can be moved, can feel emotion, then that to me is just what a thing to do with one’s life. That seems like a real honorable way to live. So yeah, I’m glad you said that, that you can hear that in that music, because that piece is very much inspired by not just the piece “Alabama” because maybe there’s some of that in that, but it’s more the ethos of taking some kind of struggle and turning it into an expression of hope, whatever it is.
